newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea C/A deficit seen at $19 bln in '96-Fin Min.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea C/A deficit seen at $19 bln in '96-Fin Min.

text.p: South Korea's Finance and Economic Ministry said on Friday it expected the country's current account deficit to rise to $19 billion in 1996 from a deficit of $8.8 billion in 1995.
The forecast was released in a report presented for parliamentary inspection. The ministry in September forecast a $15 billion shortfall for the year.
But the report did not give an explanation for the expanding deficit.

Swollen by falling prices of key exports including semiconductors, steel and petrochemicals, South Korea's current account deficit totalled $15.24 billion for the first eight months of 1996, more than doubling a $7.33 billion shortfall in the same period of last year.
The ministry also said it expected the country's overall balance of payments to show a $3.0 billion deficit for 1996 from a $30.8 billion surplus a year earlier.
